name: 2-(benzylamino)-1,4-naphthoquinone
flag: route: the 2-amino N is conjugated to the quinone (poor nucleophile); the same product is normally made by adding a benzylamine / aminomethyl resin to the quinone, not by N-benzylation

name: 2-(benzyloxy)-3-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone (O-benzyl phthiocol)
flag: route: O- vs C-alkylation selectivity of the acidic 2-hydroxy-1,4-naphthoquinone enol (as for lawsone)

name: 2-[benzyl(ethyl)amino]-1,4-naphthoquinone
flag: route: tertiary enaminone; sterically hindered N-benzylation of a conjugated (weakly nucleophilic) amine

name: 2-(benzyloxy)-3-chloro-1,4-naphthoquinone
flag: stability: the ring C-Cl is a nucleophilic vinylic substitution site (amines, thiols, alkoxides) - may not survive grafting or cycling

name: 2-(benzyloxy)-3-bromo-1,4-naphthoquinone
flag: stability: the ring C-Br is a nucleophilic vinylic substitution site (amines, thiols, alkoxides) - may not survive grafting or cycling

name: 8-(benzyloxy)-2-chloro-7-ethyl-6-methoxy-1,4-naphthoquinone
flag: stability: ring C-Cl substitution site; grafting the peri 8-OH removes its intramolecular H-bond to C1=O (shifts potentials)

name: 4-(benzylamino)-3-bromo-1,2-naphthoquinone
flag: stability: o-quinone (reactive Michael acceptor) with a ring C-Br substitution site; route as for aminoquinones

name: 4-{2-[4-(benzyloxy)phenyl]propan-2-yl}-1,2-benzoquinone
flag: stability: unsubstituted o-benzoquinone positions (reactive Michael acceptor; o-quinones of this type are known to be unstable)
